title: I Kill the Bear Premiere: Jared Keeso's New Comedy Takes on Culture Wars
text: I Kill the Bear Premiere: Jared Keeso's New Comedy Takes on Culture Wars Jared Keeso launches I Kill the Bear on November 6, featuring Georges St-Pierre and Chad Kroeger in a political comedy about wrangling modern cultural controversies. I Kill the Bear, a new comedy series created by and starring Jared Keeso, premieres on November 6 on Crave. The show centers on the Thibault family, a French-Canadian clan dedicated to training bears for film and television productions. The series has generated significant pre-launch buzz due to its high-profile casting choices. Retired UFC champion Georges St-Pierre and Nickelback frontman Chad Kroeger have joined the ensemble cast in comedic roles. Additionally, press materials confirm that actor Edward Norton appears in an early episode.Celebrity Casting and Production DetailsReports from the Sudbury production location suggested that Brad Pitt made a visit, fueling speculation about a potential reunion with his Fight Club co-stars. The official press kit verifies that Pitt will appear in the series, adding to the roster of notable guest stars.While the celebrity names draw attention, the core narrative focuses on the Thibault siblings who have carried on a hundred-year family tradition. They are preparing to close their business due to increasing conflicts with a group referred to as New Hollywood. The show explores the tensions between traditional values and modern social media sensibilities.Political Themes and Cultural CommentaryThe series serves as a parable addressing the contemporary culture wars. The Thibault family displays explicit rules for life on their walls and uses whiteboards to teach lessons about social conduct. The primary advice includes quitting social media, avoiding internet pornography, showing respect to others, and channeling anger through hard rock music.These messages are presented through the character of Gabby Thibault, played by Jared Keeso. He is depicted as a quiet and withdrawn man who struggles with modern taboos. The show highlights moments where his lack of awareness regarding current social norms leads to comedic conflict with others.Character Dynamics and New Hollywood ConflictThe narrative introduces Timothy and Rose, characters played by Dylan Playfair and Eliana Jones. They represent the New Hollywood perspective and quickly label the Thibaults' attitudes as unacceptable. The conflict escalates when they devise a plan to spread rumors to protect themselves from online cancellation.Andrée Thibault, portrayed by Sarah-Maude Beauchesne, explains the family's history to a documentarian. She describes her brothers as distinct individuals: the goofy Cedric played by Jonathan Torrens, the brooding Olivier played by Georges St-Pierre, and the withdrawn Gabby. The family has worked on major films like The Revenant and Legends of the Fall before deciding to shut down.Comedy Style and Critical ReceptionChad Kroeger appears as Son of Grizzly Adams, a less ethical wrangler who serves as a foil to the Thibaults. His character wears a bear-fur coat and a pimp hat, providing some of the show's funniest moments. The comedy relies heavily on the dynamic between Keeso and Torrens, who trade rapid-fire dialogue in cod French accents.Critics note that while some gags about political incorrectness feel dated, the overall production remains engaging. The show divides characters into cliques much like Keeso's previous work on Letterkenny. It aims to provoke thought about how society handles disagreement and censorship in the digital age.

The primary advice includes quitting social media, avoiding internet pornography, showing respect to others, and channeling anger through hard rock music.These messages are presented through the character of Gabby Thibault, played by Jared Keeso.
